Sergio — thanks, attached is the tighter export for Aug 18–25 with request_id and api_key columns. We also ran an internal audit and found an automated prefetch job (job id: prefetch-weekly-PRD) that was mistakenly pointed at the production API key for a subset of customer IDs. We had intended that job to point at a sandbox endpoint.

Key details:
- Range: 2026-08-20 03:00 to 2026-08-21 06:00 UTC
- Approx requests: 2.1M (duplicate-replay behavior observed)
- API keys mixed: includes one prod key and two sandbox keys

I'm attaching a screenshot of our internal audit (audit_screenshot.png) showing the job config and timestamps. We can also export full request_id lists if you want to correlate on your logs.

Given this, procurement wants the collection paused until we have final reconciliation. We appreciate a quick forensic read and a provisional credit if the duplicate requests are on our side.

-Mike

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Mike Burns <mike.burns@crestlinehealth.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Strange spike on August usage - invoice hold request

Mike / Sergio — Connor from Finance here. We've completed a quick forensic pairing between Crestline's request_ids (from the Aug 18–25 export) and Redwood's metering. Summary below; full notes attached.

Findings (high level):
- Match rate: 98.6% of the exported Crestline request_ids map to Redwood metering entries in the Aug 20 03:00–Aug 21 06:00 UTC window.
- Root cause: Crestline's prefetch-weekly-PRD job iterated a customer list twice due to a missing dedupe guard; the job used a production API key for the first loop and then retried the same list with the prod key again, causing near-duplicate requests.
- Impact: ~2.05M extra requests attributed to the prod key during that window. The requests were valid calls (not system bug on Redwood).

Proposed remediation & collection path:
1) Put the invoice on hold until Sep 23, 2026 while Crestline completes a final export / reconciliation (you have our pause already).
2) Apply a provisional credit equal to 40% of the disputed overage line while we finalize a targeted reconciliation. This is based on precedent where duplicate-orchestration incidents split responsibility; we're open to adjusting if Crestline provides a narrower list of request_ids to subtract.
3) If Crestline provides a definitive request_id list for the duplicate run, we will do a precise retro-bill and issue a prorated credit or final invoice correction.

Next steps:
- Mike: please confirm whether Crestline will provide the final request_id list by EOD Sep 20.
- Kimberly: I'll queue the provisional credit and collection hold (staffing notes attached).
